title: What a year in space did to Scott Kelly's body 🚀
subject: astronaut
description:
Would you spend a year in space for this? 👇

NASA's Twins Study compared astronaut Scott Kelly, after 340 days on the International Space Station, with his identical twin Mark on Earth. His spine stretched, his telomeres lengthened and then shortened within 48 hours of landing, and about 91% of his gene expression changes returned to baseline.

Sources: NASA ("NASA's Twins Study Results Published in Science", 2019), The Physiological Society / Vernice, Bailey & Mason ("Telomeres and genomic instability during long-duration spaceflight"), Spaceflight Now ("Kelly describes re-adaptation to gravity", 2016)
tags: what space does to your body
how space changes the human body

scenes.text: You can come back from space 2 inches taller.
Scott Kelly did after 340 days on the space station, while his twin Mark stayed home.
With no gravity squeezing his spine, it stretched. His telomeres, the caps on his chromosomes, grew too.
Within 48 hours of landing, they shortened sharply.
His skin was a problem too. It hadn't touched anything for so long, he said, it was very, very sensitive.
About 91 percent of his gene activity changes reversed. A few lingered 6 months later.
